title: Shepherd's Pie
description: A comforting bake of minced lamb in rich gravy under a golden mashed potato crust.
steps: Peel and chop the potatoes, then boil until tender.
Fry the onion and carrots until soft, then brown the mince alongside them.
Stir in the tomato puree and flour, then pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter and milk, then season.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish, top with the mash and scatter over the cheddar.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

title: Full English Breakfast
description: A hearty fried breakfast of sausages, bacon, eggs and all the trimmings.
steps: Fry the sausages in a splash of oil over medium heat until browned all over, about 12 minutes.
Add the bacon and mushrooms to the pan and fry until crisp and golden.
Push everything to one side of the pan and fry the tomatoes and eggs alongside.
Warm the baked beans through in a small saucepan.
Toast the bread.
Plate everything together, season with salt and pepper, and serve with the toast.

title: Bangers and Mash
description: Pork sausages with buttery mash and a rich onion gravy.
steps: Grill or fry the sausages until browned and cooked through, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender.
Melt the butter and cook the onions slowly until soft and golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir the flour into the onions, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce, simmering until thickened.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Serve the sausages on the mash, smothered in onion gravy.

title: Oven Fish and Chips
description: Oven-baked battered fish with thick-cut chips, a lighter take on the takeaway classic.
steps: Toss the chips in oil and salt and spread out on a baking tray.
Roast the chips at 220°C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, beer and salt into a smooth batter.
Dip the fish fillets in the batter and place on a lined tray.
Bake the fish alongside the chips for the final 15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Serve the fish and chips together with a wedge of lemon.

title: Beef and Ale Stew
description: Beef chunks slow-braised in ale with root vegetables until meltingly tender.
steps: Toss the beef in the flour and brown in batches in hot oil, then set aside.
Fry the onion, carrots and celery in the same pot until softened.
Return the beef to the pot and stir in the tomato puree.
Pour in the ale and stock, add the bay leaves, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender.
Season with salt and pepper before serving.

title: Leek and Potato Soup
description: A smooth, buttery soup of leeks and potatoes, ready in well under an hour.
steps: Melt the butter and gently cook the leeks and onion until soft, without browning.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Blend the soup until smooth.
Stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper.
Warm through gently and serve.

title: Macaroni Cheese
description: Pasta baked in a rich cheese sauce with a crisp golden crust.
steps: Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender, then drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then whisk in the milk until smooth.
Simmer the sauce until thickened, then stir in the cheddar and mustard powder until melted.
Fold the macaroni through the cheese sauce and season with salt.
Transfer to a baking dish, scatter over the breadcrumbs and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until golden.

title: Toad in the Hole
description: Pork sausages baked in a crisp Yorkshire pudding batter, served with onion gravy.
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest for 20 minutes.
Put the oil and sausages in a roasting tin and roast at 220°C for 10 minutes until the oil is very hot.
Pour the batter around the sausages and return to the oven for 25 minutes until well risen and golden.
Meanwhile, fry the onion until soft, stir in the flour, then add the stock and simmer into a gravy.
Serve the toad in the hole straight from the tin with the onion gravy.

title: Sausage Rolls
description: Flaky puff pastry parcels around a well-seasoned sausage filling, best served warm.
steps: Mix the sausage meat with the onion, sage, salt and pepper.
Unroll the pastry and spoon the filling along one edge in a long log.
Roll the pastry around the filling and seal the edge with a little beaten egg.
Cut into six rolls and brush the tops with the remaining egg.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden.

title: Coronation Chicken Sandwiches
description: Cold roast chicken in a mild curried mayonnaise with sultanas, piled into sandwiches.
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, mango chutney and curry powder together.
Fold in the shredded chicken and sultanas and season with salt.
Spread the mixture generously over half the bread slices.
Top with the remaining bread and press down gently.
Cut the sandwiches in half to serve.

title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
description: A light sponge soaked in a tangy lemon syrup and finished with a crisp sugar glaze.
steps: Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour, baking powder and lemon zest.
Spoon the batter into a lined loaf tin and bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Mix the lemon juice with the sugar for the drizzle.
Prick the warm cake all over and pour over the drizzle, letting it soak in and set into a crust.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: A rich date sponge in a caramel sauce, served warm as the definitive British dessert.
steps: Simmer the dates in the water for 5 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda and set aside to cool slightly.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour and the date mixture.
Pour the batter into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes until risen and firm.
Melt the butter, sugar and cream together for the sauce, stirring until smooth and glossy.
Pour half the sauce over the warm pudding and serve the rest alongside.
